whyNow.title: Why Verified Impact Matters
whyNow.subtitle: The gap is not funding. The gap is trust. Unprecedented convergence of regulatory pressure, ESG momentum, and digital capability creates the defining moment for accountability.
whyNow.deadlineDesc: With only 4 years until the UN SDG deadline, tracking and verifying progress is existential. Every unverified claim is a missed opportunity for real impact.
whyNow.momentumDesc: IFRS S1/S2 sustainability disclosure standards are becoming law globally. Nigeria's FRC SRG1 2026 requires compliance. Organizations need systems, not spreadsheets.
whyNow.digitalDesc: 600M+ mobile users across Africa enable community-driven verification at scale. The technology to prove impact finally exists.
whyNow.esgDesc: Billions are invested into development every year, yet much of that impact remains unverified, fragmented, or overstated. Institutions demand proof, not reports.

gettingStarted.q1: How do I create an account?
gettingStarted.a1: Click 'Sign Up' on the homepage. You can register with email, Google, or GitHub. After registration, you'll be prompted to complete your profile and select your primary role (citizen reporter, NGO, government, or corporate).
gettingStarted.q2: How do I submit a development project report?
gettingStarted.a2: Navigate to 'Submit Report' from the sidebar. Fill out the project details including title, description, location (with GPS coordinates), SDG alignment, and supporting documentation. Your report starts at 'Self-Report' verification level and can be upgraded through community verification.
gettingStarted.q3: What are the different user roles?
gettingStarted.a3: DevMapper has 5 primary roles: Citizen Reporter (default), NGO Representative, Government Official, Corporate Representative, and Platform Admin. Each role has different verification capabilities. For example, only government officials can provide Level 4 'Institutional Verification'.
gettingStarted.a4: Yes! The Free tier allows you to submit up to 3 projects per month, use Kanban and List views, and access basic analytics. Paid plans (Lite, Pro, Advanced, Enterprise) unlock features like Gantt charts, Ndovu Akili AI (Copilot), ESG modules, and higher project quotas.

reportingVerification.q1: How is data verified on the platform?
reportingVerification.a1: We use a 5-level verification system: 1) Self-Report (submitted by project owner), 2) Citizen Verification (community members confirm), 3) NGO Verification (organization validates), 4) Government Verification (official institutional confirmation), and 5) Platform Audit (automated cross-referencing and expert review).
reportingVerification.q2: Can I edit or update my submitted reports?
reportingVerification.a2: Yes. Go to 'My Projects', select the project, and use 'Update Progress' to add milestones, budget updates, indicator data, and photo evidence. All updates maintain an audit trail visible to verifiers.
reportingVerification.q3: How do I verify someone else's project?
reportingVerification.a3: Navigate to the project page and click 'Verify'. Your verification level is automatically determined by your role. You must provide written comments and optionally upload evidence. You cannot verify your own projects.
reportingVerification.q4: What happens when a project is flagged?
reportingVerification.a4: Flagged projects enter a review queue. A moderator examines the flag within 48 hours. If the flag is valid, the project may be suspended pending correction. The reporter receives notification and can respond or appeal.
reportingVerification.q5: How do SDG and Agenda 2063 alignment work?
reportingVerification.a5: When submitting a project, select the relevant SDG goals (1–17). The platform automatically maps these to AU Agenda 2063 aspirations. The SDG-Agenda 2063 dashboard shows alignment density, gap analysis, and country-level filtering.

projectManagement.q1: What PM features are available on the Free plan?
projectManagement.a1: Free users get Kanban Board and List View with basic task management. You can create tasks, set priorities, and track status (to-do, in-progress, done). Gantt Chart, resource allocation, and Ndovu Akili AI (Copilot) require Lite+ or Pro+ plans.
projectManagement.q2: How does the Gantt Chart view work?
projectManagement.a2: Available on Lite+ plans. The Gantt Chart visualizes project timelines, task dependencies, and milestone dates. Tasks are displayed as horizontal bars with drag-to-reschedule support. It integrates directly with your project milestones from Supabase.
projectManagement.q3: Can I assign tasks to team members?
projectManagement.a3: Yes, on Lite+ plans and above. Task assignment uses the project affiliation system — only users who are affiliated with a project (owner, partner, funder) can be assigned tasks. Assignees receive notifications.
projectManagement.q4: What is the Ndovu Akili AI (Copilot)?
projectManagement.a4: Available on Pro+ plans. The Ndovu Akili AI assists with compliance gap analysis, report drafting, and general development questions. It has context-aware modes for different use cases and maintains conversation history.

esgCompliance.q1: How do I access ESG features?
esgCompliance.a1: ESG modules are available for organizations on Pro plans and above with esg_enabled set to true. Navigate to 'ESG Dashboard' from the sidebar to access emissions tracking, supplier management, scenario analysis, and regulatory exposure profiles.
esgCompliance.q2: How does Scope 3 emissions tracking work?
esgCompliance.a2: Import your suppliers via CSV or manual entry. The platform calculates Scope 3 emissions based on supplier activity data, emission factors, and industry benchmarks. Data quality is tracked (estimated vs. measured vs. verified) to ensure transparency.
esgCompliance.q3: What regulatory frameworks does the Rule Engine cover?
esgCompliance.a3: The Rule Engine matches your organization's profile (country, actor type, sector) against stored regulatory frameworks. It covers mandatory ESG disclosure requirements, climate reporting mandates, and voluntary frameworks like GRI and TCFD across African jurisdictions.

billingPlans.a1: We offer 5 tiers: Free (3 projects/month), Lite ($5/month, 10 projects), Pro ($15/month, 40 projects + ESG), Advanced ($30/month, 150 projects + full features), and Enterprise (custom pricing, unlimited). Scholarships are available for qualifying organizations.
billingPlans.q2: How do I apply for a scholarship?
billingPlans.a2: Go to Settings → Billing → Apply for Scholarship. Provide your organization details, mission statement, and proof of eligibility. Scholarships grant Pro-tier access at no cost for qualifying NGOs, community organizations, and educational institutions.
billingPlans.a3: We accept payments via Flutterwave and Paystack, supporting credit/debit cards, mobile money (M-Pesa, MTN MoMo), bank transfers, and USSD across African currencies (NGN, KES, ZAR, GHS, UGX, TZS, etc.).
billingPlans.a4: Each plan has a monthly project quota that refreshes on your billing date. Pro+ plans support rollover — unused quota carries to the next month (up to your plan cap). Quota status is visible in your dashboard.

carbonSustainability.q1: How do I track carbon emissions for a project?
carbonSustainability.a1: Open any project in Project Management, then navigate to the 'Carbon' tab. Enter Scope 1 (direct), Scope 2 (energy), and Scope 3 (supply chain) emissions in tonnes CO2e. The platform calculates total footprint and tracks reduction over time.
carbonSustainability.a2: The Circularity Score measures how well a project reuses materials and diverts waste. It is calculated as: (waste_diverted + material_reused) / total_waste × 100. Scores above 50% indicate good circular economy practices.
carbonSustainability.a3: The Compliance tab tracks Paris Agreement Article 6 readiness. It assesses ITMO (Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes) eligibility, corresponding adjustments, and country-of-origin compliance. This helps projects participate in international carbon markets.
carbonSustainability.q4: Can I generate carbon credits from my project?
carbonSustainability.a4: Yes. Use the 'Carbon Assets' tab to register verified emission reductions. Credits can be tracked through their lifecycle: generation, ownership transfer, and retirement. Each credit includes methodology, vintage year, and verification status.

technicalIssues.q1: The map isn't loading. What should I do?
technicalIssues.a1: Maps require a stable internet connection. Try: 1) Refresh the page, 2) Clear browser cache, 3) Try a different browser. If maps consistently fail, check if your organization has firewall rules blocking MapLibre or Leaflet tile servers.
technicalIssues.q2: How do I reset my password?
technicalIssues.a2: Click 'Forgot Password' on the login page. Enter your email and you'll receive a password reset link. The link expires in 10 minutes. If you signed up with Google or GitHub, use those providers to log in instead.
technicalIssues.a3: DevMapper is a Progressive Web App (PWA). You can install it to your home screen for quick access. Basic viewing works offline, but submitting reports and syncing data requires an internet connection.
technicalIssues.q4: My report submission failed. What happened?
technicalIssues.a4: Common causes: 1) Project quota exhausted (check plan limits), 2) Missing required fields (title, description, location, SDG goal, status), 3) Network timeout. Check the error message for specifics and try again.
technicalIssues.q5: How do I connect to my organization?
technicalIssues.a5: Organizations are auto-created on sign-up. To join an existing organization, contact the organization admin who can add you via the Admin Dashboard. Organization membership determines your plan tier and project quota.
